canonical_sequence: Rowan Pike believed the next morning's controller migration would erase Iris Venn's original hand-timed pulse sequence.
After Mara denied a forty-eight-hour estate review, Rowan decided to hide Aurora Circuit until the estate could force a technical review.
Rowan prepared a polarized insert from a catalog image before the gala.
Rowan entered Gallery 3 alone under the authorized catalog work order while the case was in calibration mode.
Rowan taped over the rear contact sensor and opened the service panel at 9:42:11 p.m.; frame RP_2207 captured the open panel at 9:42:14 p.m.
Rowan removed Aurora Circuit from the plinth at 9:42:18 p.m.
Rowan placed the insert in the smart-glass guide and concealed the 1.84-kilogram sculpture in his hard equipment case.
The scheduled blackout later rebooted the smart glass, exposed the flat insert, and caused staff to discover the earlier theft.

claim_rules.description: The artwork was removed before the planned blackout.
The rear service-panel contact was deliberately bypassed.
A polarized image concealed the empty display until the glass rebooted.
Rowan was the only suspect with access at the actual removal time.
Rowan's statement about remaining behind the brass line conflicts with his camera record.
Rowan's case gained the artwork's mass while remaining under his control.
Rowan wanted to prevent the irreversible loss of Iris Venn's original timing and buy time for estate review.
The blackout executed automatically and exposed rather than enabled the theft.

exoneration_rules.summary: The removal occurred while Mara was continuously visible in the greenroom.
Theo was in the booth at the removal time, and the later blackout was automatic.
Nia's body camera places her at the loading bay when the plinth lost its load.

hints: Treat the blackout as the discovery time, not the removal time.
Compare the artwork's mass with the two equipment-case measurements.
Ask what was scheduled to disappear the morning after the gala—and who cared enough to delay it.
